text: In plural first-order logic, how is the atomic formula x ≺ xx read?
choices: x is a subset of xx
x is a member of the set xx
x is one of the xx
explanation: x ≺ xx is read 'x is one of the xx,' relating a single individual to some individuals taken plurally. It is not set membership (∈) — xx is not a set, so 'subset' and 'member of the set' both wrongly reify a set — and it is not identity, since x is just one object among the several xx.
